title: A tenth is smaller than a fifth

interactive.brief: The one thing you should see is every piece on the bar shrink, from 200 mm at 5 pieces to 100 mm at 10, when you raise the number of equal pieces the metre is cut into.

explain.text:
More equal pieces in one whole means smaller pieces. Each piece is 1000 mm ÷ pieces: 5 give 200 mm, 10 give 100 mm. When the tops match, the bigger bottom is the smaller fraction.[^1][^2]

The trap is the whole-number habit: 10 is more than 5, so 1/10 looks bigger.[^3] But if a tenth were over 200 mm, ten of them would make more than 2000 mm from one metre.

**Same whole, more pieces, smaller pieces: a tenth of a metre, 100 mm, is shorter than a fifth.**

analogy.text: Matching lamps in series on 230 V share it: two get 115 V each, ten get 23 V. More lamps, less each.
analogy.breaks: Only in series: in parallel each lamp sees near enough the full 230 V.

practice.text:
**Rule of thumb:** same whole, same top: bigger bottom, smaller piece.

**Worked example:** 2400 mm of trunking in equal bays. 2400 ÷ 4 = 600 mm; 2400 ÷ 8 = 300 mm. More bays, shorter bays.

**Common mistakes**
- Thinking 1/10 beats 1/5 because 10 beats 5.
- Using the rule when the tops differ: 3/10 beats 1/5.

sources.quote: Unit fractions can be compared and ordered by looking at the denominator. The greater the denominator, the smaller the fraction.
